style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression down a modern apparel distribution warehouse aisle: towering weathered-orange pallet racking on the left packed solid with shrink-wrapped corrugated cartons of folded apparel stock, while the facing rack row stands stripped to bare galvanised steel beams holding a few empty pallets. Hard directional daylight pours from the loading bay doors at the far right end, raking across carton faces and casting long rack shadows over polished concrete. Weathered orange, bone white and graphite palette, crisp crystalline air, deep industrial contrast, flat compressed layers of stacked stock receding to a bright doorway. Extreme asymmetry: the loaded stock wall commands the left two-thirds with the aisle breathing to the right. No people. Fine film grain.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, legible words, numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: The stake in this story is scale: $1.1 billion of inventory still standing after a 50% assortment cut. Telephoto compression stacks rack layer over rack layer into a dense wall of stock, so the reader physically feels the mass the purge leaves behind, while the stripped facing row states the halving without a single invented prop. Macro would strip the environment from a systemic capacity story, and the warehouse aisle is where this planning decision actually lands.
subject: a towering pallet-rack aisle of shrink-wrapped apparel cartons — the standing inventory — beside a rack row stripped half empty
core_thesis: Under Armour's 50% SKU purge simplifies the forecast once, but its shelves still carry $1.1 billion of inventory, 4% above plan — the durable payoff comes from faster decisions on what each remaining SKU is becoming, every cycle after.
core_conflict: one-time assortment simplification vs. recurring demand misses — the SKU count halves while revenue falls 7% and stock lands above plan, so the purge pays once but the inventory line keeps refilling every quarter
composition: extreme asymmetry — the loaded stock wall commands the left two-thirds of the frame, the aisle recedes toward a bright loading bay on the right
